Latin word

ēmendō

ēmendō, ēmendāre, ēmendāvī, ēmendātum

verb, first conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

correct (a text, a piece of work), free from mistakes; correct or amend; correct, emend (a text); improve, correct, free from faults; reform, amend, correct

In this lexicon

  • correct

    also used · classical · Quint. 2.2.5: quae ēmendanda erunt; Traupman 29, 246; Traupman 297

  • debug

    the recommended word · * our formation

  • edit

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 2.16 fin.; Quint. 2.2.7 (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. edit (prepare a text for publication)

  • improve

    the recommended word · classical · Sen. Ep. 6.1: nōn ēmendārī mē tantum sed trānsfigūrārī; Cic. Leg. 3.30 (Lewis & Short): tōta cīvitās ēmendārī et corrigī solet continentiā prīncipum; Traupman 154; Traupman 332

  • reform

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Leg. 3.30: sīc ēmendārī et corrigī continentiā; Hor. Ep. 2.1.3: lēgibus ēmendēs; Traupman 157, 370

  • revise

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.16.4 (Lewis & Short); Quint. 2.2.7 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • corrige, sōdēs, hoc … et hoc

    fix this, please … and thisHor. Ars 438–439

    In the entry for edit

  • quaedam īnstituī, quae līmantur ā mē polītius

    I have begun some things, which I am polishing with more careCic. Ac. 1.2 (Lewis & Short)

    In the entry for edit

  • Quīdam sedent ad mēnsam, et scrībunt; ipse corrigit mendās.

    Some sit at the table and write; the master himself corrects the mistakes.Comen. OP 97

    In the entry for edit

  • legere et ēmendāre

    to proofreadTraupman 366

    In the entry for edit

  • Intellegō, Lūcīlī, nōn ēmendārī mē tantum sed trānsfigūrārī.

    I can see, Lucilius, that I am not just being improved but transformed.Sen. Ep. 6.1

    In the entry for improve

  • Ex vitiō alius sapiēns ēmendat suum.

    From another’s fault the wise man corrects his own.Publ. E 4

    In the entry for improve

  • vitium … uxōris aut tollendum aut ferendum est. quī tollit vitium, uxōrem commodiōrem praestat, quī fert, sēsē meliōrem facit

    A wife’s fault must be either cured or borne: whoever cures it makes his wife easier to live with; whoever bears it makes himself better.Gell. 1.17.4 (Varro)

    In the entry for improve

  • cum tot sustineās et tanta negōtia sōlus, rēs Ītalās armīs tūtēris, mōribus ōrnēs, lēgibus ēmendēs

    since you alone carry so many and such great burdens, guarding Italy with arms, gracing her with morals, reforming her with lawsHor. Ep. 2.1.1–3

    In the entry for reform

  • ut enim cupiditātibus prīncipum et vitiīs īnficī solet tōta cīvitās, sīc ēmendārī et corrigī continentiā
